deck: SpaceX continues its Starship saga while ULA faces financial woes.

stories.head: SpaceX's 13th Starship flight outpaces airlines
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched its 13th Starship test flight, deploying operational satellites while addressing past issues. At this pace, they may soon have more test flights than American Airlines has daily departures. The relentless pursuit of testing has become a hallmark of their strategy.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can keep this up, they'll redefine what it means to be operational in the launch market.

stories.head: ULA's Vulcan woes lead to financial strain
stories.body: United Launch Alliance is grappling with significant financial challenges due to the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. This situation has reportedly led to a reevaluation of contracts and a potential cash flow crisis, highlighting that even industry giants can falter when their launch vehicles are sidelined.
stories.soWhat: If ULA can't get Vulcan off the ground soon, it may lose its edge to more agile competitors.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense demand
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in Series C funding, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This investment underscores the increasing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness solutions, particularly from the Department of Defense, which is keen on enhancing its capabilities.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's success illustrates that in today's market, cash often speaks louder than actual innovation.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on ULA's recovery plans
watchlist.body: With financial pressures mounting, ULA's next steps could redefine its competitive landscape in the coming weeks.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX's next Starship test
watchlist.body: Another Starship test could further cement SpaceX's dominance in the launch sector if successful.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's strategic partnerships
watchlist.body: As True Anomaly scales, its partnerships with defense agencies will be crucial to watch for future contracts.

watchlist.title: Implications of the FY27 budget increase
watchlist.body: The additional $1.4 billion for space resilience could lead to increased opportunities for contractors in the defense space.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.

tickers.note: Virgin Galactic's stock remains stagnant as commercial space tourism is still a distant dream.
Lockheed Martin's focus on space resilience is aligning well with the increased defense budget.
Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program shows the government is still a lucrative client.
Aerojet Rocketdyne's recent contracts are a reminder that propulsion systems remain a hot commodity.
